caption:
At 17, Tony Robbins left home. He worked as a janitor. And he sold tickets to someone else's seminars.

Jim Rohn's.

He wasn't the speaker. He was the guy filling the room for a speaker who already had a name.

That's the part of the story that gets skipped, and it's the only part that transfers.

He learned how to work a room — how to move people, handle an objection, close — years before he had anything of his own to say in one.

Unlimited Power came in 1986. Awaken the Giant Within in 1991. The product arrived after the skill, not before it.

Most people do it the other way round. They build the thing first and assume they'll figure out selling later. Then the thing is finished and nobody buys it, and they decide the market was wrong.

Learning to sell is not something you bolt on at the end. It's the thing that tells you what's worth building.

📌 Send this to someone who's great at what they do and hates selling it. This is the gap costing them the most.
